title: Release Murmuration — Warmup tactics & pinning scratchpad
content:
Context and intent:
- Quick personal scratchpad for a gentle, observability-first warmup pattern I want to try for model flips/quantized-variant rollouts. Name inspired by how a murmuration of starlings moves in waves — small cohorts that change direction quickly with telemetry as the guide.

High-level goals:
- Minimize user-visible regressions (latency, hallucination spikes, token cost surprises).
- Keep burn predictable: prefer many short micro-cohorts over one long canary where telemetry drifts unnoticed.
- Make pinning decisions reversible and auditable (timestamp, client set, reason).

Core vocabulary (my shorthand):
- murmur: one micro-cohort window (typical 15–60 min depending on traffic density).
- feather: priming step to warm KV cache and embeddings for a cohort before flipping live traffic.
- anchor: a small persistent holdback group used as ground truth for quality drift detection.
- pin: force a given client or client group to a model version for a duration.

Warmup choreography (sequence):
1) Preflight (T-1 to T-0):
   - Create rollout artifact: version tags + provenance (git sha, quantization profile).
   - Run static smoke on a replay corpus: perf / top-10 tokens distribution / simple eval prompts (10–20).
   - Prepare feather job: synthetic requests to populate KV cache, prime embeddings, and fill common prompts. Duration: 3–10m per replica.
2) Murmur phase 1 (0.1% traffic; 15m):
   - Route 0.1% traffic across 5 geographically spread clients (if available).
   - Observe P50/P95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost delta, and two quality signals: anchor vs murmur fuzz distance (see below).
   - Run synthetic aligned tests every 5 minutes.
3) Murmur phase 2 (0.5% traffic; 30m):
   - Expand to broader client set; run feather for new replicas before flip.
4) Murmur phase 3 (2% traffic; 60m):
   - If green, widen to 5% for 2h; otherwise rollback to previous stable.
5) Gradual ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%):
   - Steps should take at least 30m for any multi-region step but can be shorter if traffic is low.

Safety gates / signals (immediate rollback if any are violated):
- Latency: P95 > baseline P95 + 30% (or absolute > 800ms) for 2 consecutive murmur windows.
- Errors: 5xx rate > baseline 5xx * 3 or >0.5% absolute.
- Cost: per-token cost delta > expected quantization saving * 0.5 (unusual but keep an eye).
- Quality: anchor divergence metric > 0.12 (see quick metric below) or any customer-reported semantic regression from CS.
- Observability gap: if any telemetry source lags by >5m, pause and triage.

Quick metric idea: anchor vs murmur fuzz distance
- Select anchor group (persistent clients pinned to stable model). For every murmur sample, compute embedding distance between anchor and murmur outputs on a fixed evaluation prompt set (40 prompts). Aggregate median cosine distance and track delta vs baseline. Conservative threshold for my experiments: median delta > 0.08 triggers manual review; >0.12 auto-pause.

Pinning heuristics (practical rules):
- Pin durations: default 24h for investigative pins, 1–2h for fast rollback experiments.
- Pin reasons recorded: regression-investigation | perf-hedge | compliance | debug.
- When pinning a client: annotate client tag (e.g., client-team:mobile-beta) + incident link.

Feather patterns (to avoid cold-start spikes):
- Start feathering 10m before opening a murmur window for any region/replica.
- Synthetic feeder should mimic common prompt prefixes and include the 40-eval set.
- If using persistent KV stores, perform small key reads/writes that mimic production key shapes.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout quick runbook):
- [ ] Upload rollout artifact with notes and link to PR
- [ ] Create murmur schedule in calendar and notify SRE for on-call alignment
- [ ] Ensure dashboards for P50/P95, 5xx, cost-per-token, anchor-fuzz are pinned and shared
- [ ] Start feathering 10m prior to murmur phase 1
- [ ] Confirm synthetic test harness running and visible
- [ ] Slack channel: #rollouts-live notify start and expected checkpoints

Edge cases and things to watch (notes to self):
- Client affinity: some clients have session-affinity semantics that break quick pin flips. Prefer SDK-driven model pin flags for those clients.
- Region imbalance: small murmur % in a low-traffic region can be noisy; prefer absolute-request thresholds (min 50 reqs per murmur window) rather than pure percentage.
- Cold-model memory pressure: if new quantized variant increases peak memory on host, SRE will need headroom; set a host-level safety buffer (e.g., 15% spare GPU memory) during ramp.
- Retries: client-side retries can amplify failures; instrument idempotency tokens and watch retry amplification ratio (requests resulting in >1 server call).

Hypotheses I want to validate with this pattern:
- Micro-cohorts with feathering reduce the probability of undetected regressions versus a single long canary.
- Embedding-based anchor fuzz is a sensitive early-warning for semantic drift when small output changes are present but hard to detect via simple error percentages.
- Pin durations <2h accelerate triage because they force explicit decisions (keep or revert) instead of letting a model drift for days.

Open questions / To do:
- Decide concrete anchor prompt set (need volunteers from evaluation team).
- Implement a lightweight anchor-fuzz job in experiments infra (file a ticket).
- Try one non-quantized -> quantized flip next week in staging using this choreography.

Random scribbles (for archive):
- If murmur pattern works, think about a UI that shows current "murmuration map": cohort size, feather status, anchor delta.
- Consider an automated cool-off if cost drift is > expected saving/2 and quality delta small — revert to cheaper variant automatically.

End of scratchpad.

Notes: messy, intentionally — this is my running brain dump. If it becomes useful we can formalize into a proper runbook and add to Confluence.
